reviewSurface: Isolated Google Chrome headless session controlled through the Chrome DevTools Protocol against local Vite and Express servers

clippedDecorativeElements: The intentionally oversized aria-hidden backdrop orbit is clipped by the app shell and does not increase document width.

themeEvidence.visualResult: Dark Cosmic Sunrise Workshop tokens rendered legibly across the complete mission, resources, invalid-route boundary, API error state, and footer.

keyboardEvidence.resourceControls: native links with visible global focus treatment

failureRecoveryEvidence.failureMethod: Chrome network interception blocked the Vite /api proxy URL without changing application source or server state.
failureRecoveryEvidence.errorHeading: The mission could not be reached.

additionalEvidence.canonicalTitle: Define the developer identity and learning contract
additionalEvidence.invalidRoute: A direct load of /curriculum/1.5 rendered the focused whole-number boundary without curriculum content.
additionalEvidence.directRouteRepair: The first final pass found Vite treating a dotted curriculum path as file-like before React loaded. A scoped HTML fallback was added for /curriculum/*, Vite was restarted, and the full browser pass then succeeded.
additionalEvidence.resourceLinks: Both canonical HTTPS links exposed target=_blank and rel=noopener noreferrer.
additionalEvidence.console: A clean-profile rerun after adding the code-native favicon recorded no application console errors, warnings, JavaScript exceptions, or Chrome log errors across success, invalid-route, simulated API-unavailable, and retry-recovery states.
additionalEvidence.sourceFidelity: The live page showed the canonical Day 1 title, exact 30-minute schedule, two resources, Recovery win, and optional Stretch.

notes: The full-page 1280px and 320px screenshots were visually inspected. Text, cards, schedules, Recovery/Stretch labels, resource controls, and footer content remained legible without overlap or horizontal document overflow. Evidence is source-bound; pnpm test:e2e fails if reviewed browser/API/contract/curriculum source changes without a fresh pass.
